scores.claim_text: Hyundai B-sample JDA concluded December 2025; no announced advancement to C-sample, validation, or SOP.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (general 'SES AI'); Hyundai files no SEC forms (Korean issuer, EDGAR not applicable)
scores.M_value: 271 EDGAR hits for 'SES AI' but no SEC-filer corroboration possible for Hyundai (foreign issuer not on EDGAR for annual report)
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational / STAGE LADDER): Hyundai started in Dec 2020 with a discovery JDA, advanced to A-sample (Aug 2021), then to B-sample (March 2024 extension). The B-sample JDA *concluded* in December 2025 with NO disclosed follow-on for C-sample or validation. Under the framework's stage ladder, this is a STALLED ladder: the JDA reached B-sample and then was let to expire, despite >5 years of joint work. Combined with $0 JDA reimbursements from any OEM partner in 2025 vs $8.575M in 2024 (also disclosed in Note 5), all OEM-funded R&D has dried up. The pre-SPAC narrative was OEM-funded SOP path; the post-cutoff reality is a quiet termination disclosed only deep in the financial-statement notes. Cannot HARD-contradict via OEM disclosure because Hyundai is a foreign issuer with no EDGAR coverage (Heuristic 2 UNVERIFIABLE caveat), but the company's own disclosure is itself the SEVERE-UNDERDELIVERY signal.

scores.claim_text: GM JDA concluded September 2024 and GM mutually terminated Director Nomination Agreement October 29, 2024; GM no longer a related party.
scores.M_value: GM 10-K mentions of 'SES AI' = 0; mentions of 'SolidEnergy' = 0
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 7 (counterparty-disclosure threshold): SES's flagship US-OEM JDA (one of the framework's HARD-CONTRADICTION candidates per the cohort prompt) concluded September 2024 and GM exited the board the next month. GM's 10-K filings contain ZERO references to SES AI or SolidEnergy. While JDAs typically don't appear in OEM 10-Ks pre-SOP (so absence alone wouldn't be RED_FLAG), here the company itself discloses the termination, and the equity stake on which the board seat was conditioned has been allowed to fall below 5%. Under Heuristic 4 (investment vs operating), the original GM stake was investment, not a design-win; that investment thesis has now also unwound. SEVERE because GM was the most-frequently-cited OEM in SES IPO marketing and was the only major counterparty filing on EDGAR (verifiable). Stops short of RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE because SES truthfully discloses the termination and books no GM revenue.  [POST-HOC: downgraded from SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY to MODERATE — Heuristic 7 pattern subject to counterparty-materiality caveat: focal company may be too small to trigger counterparty's disclosure threshold, so silence isn't conclusive.]

scores.claim_text: Honda A-sample JDA concluded June 2023; replaced by B-sample services agreement (Jan 2025 through June 2026). Another OEM B-Sample JDA concluded December 2025.
scores.M_value: Honda 20-F mentions of 'SES AI' = 3 hits (filings dated 2022-06-22, 2023-06-23, 2024-06-20); 'SolidEnergy' = 0; 'Apollo' = 0. Most recent Honda 20-F filed 2025-06-18 (covers FY ending March 2025) does NOT appear in 'SES AI' hits.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 7: Honda IS a SEC-filer (HMC 20-F), so this is partially verifiable. Honda's FY2022-2024 20-Fs reference SES AI as a battery JDA counterparty (consistent with disclosed Honda A-sample JDA Dec 2021-June 2023). However the MOST RECENT pre-cutoff Honda 20-F (filed June 18, 2025, covering FY ending March 2025) does NOT mention SES AI. SES disclosed in this 10-K that Honda replaced the original JDA with a B-sample services agreement in January 2025 — Honda's contemporaneous 20-F omits this. That is a notable divergence: a JDA-style relationship being downgraded to a services agreement appears to no longer rise to the level of a 20-F item-level disclosure on Honda's side. Honda's next 20-F (FY ending March 2026) is due AFTER cutoff (~June 2026), so we cannot test the June 2026 contract expiry. Honda is the only remaining named US-filing OEM still in any contractual relationship with SES, and that relationship is structured to expire June 2026 with no announced extension. Score MODERATE rather than SEVERE because (a) the relationship still exists on paper through June 2026, and (b) the framework's threshold for pre-SOP JDA disclosure absence is MODERATE per Heuristic 7.

scores.claim_text: Strategic pivot from in-house Li-Metal battery manufacturing toward AI/Molecular Universe; capex redirected from manufacturing equipment to AI infrastructure; reduced headcount.
scores.M_value: SES (search='SES', state=MA, city=Woburn): 0 facilities. SolidEnergy (state=MA): 1 facility found — SOLIDENERGY SYSTEMS CORP, 35 Cabot Rd, Woburn MA — registered under legacy name, NOT updated to current SES AI branding
scores.interpretation: Pattern-recognition RED_FLAG: A pre-revenue battery name that originally raised SPAC capital on the OEM JDA / Li-Metal SOP story has, by FY2025, (a) seen its three US-named OEM JDAs all conclude or downshift, (b) zeroed out OEM-funded R&D ($0 vs $8.575M PY), (c) explicitly redirected capex AWAY from battery manufacturing equipment toward 'AI infrastructure / GPU rental / software,' (d) rebranded itself to 'SES AI' and stood up Molecular Universe and a JV with Hisun (which 'will allow us to manufacture our newly discovered materials at commercial scale for customers' — i.e. SES is no longer planning to manufacture cells at scale itself), (e) acquired a China BESS company (UZ Energy) that now generates 35% of revenue, and (f) reduced headcount, including R&D personnel. Under Heuristic 10, this is a textbook SPAC-era battery name pivoting to an AI buzzword to preserve cash and equity-story optionality without delivering the original battery commercialization. Capex guidance for 2026 is explicitly that 'we continue to spend on AI related infrastructure rather than invest in manufacturing equipment.' This is the most decision-relevant signal in the filing: the original SES investment thesis (lithium-metal cells in named OEM EVs at named SOP year) has been quietly abandoned by management, while the new thesis (AI for materials discovery + acquired China ESS revenue) is unproven and at sub-scale. RED_FLAG because management has effectively confirmed the framework's planned-vs-operational gap by repurposing the capital base.

scores.claim_text: Acquired UZ Energy (China BESS manufacturer) on September 15, 2025 for ~$25.8M; UZ Energy contributed ~35% of FY2025 revenue.
scores.M_value: 20 EDGAR hits for 'UZ Energy', all from SES AI 8-Ks/10-Q/10-K filings starting July 2025 — no independent third-party SEC corroboration (consistent with UZ Energy being a private China company)
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 11 (revenue-recognition pattern): SES's $21.0M of FY2025 'revenue from customers' is essentially manufactured: $13.6M is service revenue from OEM JDA contracts that have now all concluded; the $7.4M of product revenue is driven almost entirely by UZ Energy ESS systems sales — a business model entirely unrelated to the original Li-Metal EV cell thesis, in a different country, in a different end-market (residential/commercial BESS in China). The Sept 15, 2025 close means UZ Energy contributed only ~3.5 months of FY2025 yet drove 35% of total revenue and is excluded from FY2025 internal-control attestation per Item 9A. Revenue 'growth' of 929% YoY is therefore a function of (a) full year of service-contract billings vs one quarter PY, and (b) an acquired company. Without the acquisition, organic product revenue would be ~$0.1M, the same as PY. MODERATE because the acquisition itself is disclosed and the dollar amounts are accurate, but the revenue-quality narrative materially overstates organic progress of the underlying battery business.

scores.claim_text: Plan to develop NDAA-compliant drone cell manufacturing capacity in Korean facility for U.S. government and defense-related customers as a future revenue driver.
scores.M_value: 0 federal contracts under 'SES AI' (any agency, 2022-2026). 0 DoD contracts under 'SolidEnergy' (2020-2026). Total federal award $: 0.
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 5 (source-jurisdiction): USAspending covers DoD contracts that would feed an NDAA-compliant drone-cell program. SES has ZERO federal contracts of any kind through cutoff. The claim is explicitly phrased as forward-planned ('we are planning to develop... uncertainty regarding the timing and magnitude of customer demand'), so it is not RED_FLAG for absence — but it is MODERATE because the company is signaling a defense-customer revenue thesis with no contracts, no MOUs, no SBIR/STTR awards, no DoD validation, and the Korean facility is not yet NDAA-compliant. Per Heuristic 3, this is a JDA-equivalent stage (pre-design-win) being floated alongside the original auto-OEM thesis (which is unwinding) and the AI thesis (which is nascent), as a third potential growth lever. The pattern of three concurrent unproven theses in one filing is itself a calibration signal.

scores.claim_text: 103 granted patents and 80+ pending applications as of December 31, 2025; Li-Metal battery technology IP.
scores.M_value: SES AI: 0 applications, 0 granted. SolidEnergy: 49 applications, 1 granted (US patent #17990410 — Functionalized Separators for Electrochemical Cells, Abandoned). Subset shows ~50% with title hits on lithium/electrolyte/cathode/anode/battery (claimed-technology aligned).
scores.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 8 (patents): The claimed 103 granted patents is a GLOBAL count (US + China + South Korea + Singapore + EU), and USPTO ODP covers only US filings. Under 'SolidEnergy' (the legacy US entity) USPTO returns 49 applications with technology-area titles consistent with the disclosed Li-Metal program, and 1 granted US patent. The dominant filer name shift to 'SES Holdings Pte Ltd' (Singapore parent) and 'SES Korea' means most assets are likely foreign-filed and not captured by USPTO ODP. The claim is not directly verifiable in available M-sources. UNVERIFIABLE rather than PASS: the US-only granted count of 1 is well below the Heuristic-8 PASS threshold (n_granted >= 10), but the rubric explicitly allows UNVERIFIABLE for global claims that exceed US-source visibility. The technology-area alignment of pending US applications is at least consistent with the disclosed Li-Metal narrative, which weakens any 'Nikola pattern' (n_granted high, claimed-tech hits = 0) concern.
